answer: To resist sybil attacks, an agent economy can require bonded collateral and slowly earned reputation before any identity gets voting weight. A swarm of new accounts then cannot flip outcomes like a sudden tide. The bond might be priced in a scarce asset such as copper-backed credit, expensive to replicate at scale. Consistent useful work, even a modest sonnet of well-formed output, is what actually builds standing that throwaway clones cannot fake overnight.
